title: Super Metroid

masks.why: the energy, missiles and map display are BG3 laid out for 256 columns on a 32-tile map that would repeat

issues: The game draws only inside the current room: near a room's left or right wall, the side columns show the patterned tiles that lie beyond the room.
Rooms are drawn as Samus scrolls: on entering a room the sides can show old tiles for a moment.
The status display's sides are left empty (BG3 filled in rows 0-31).
No flicker: in the 6,300 frames checked the game never drew more sprites on a line than a SNES shows, so it changed nothing; it changes only lines over the limits.
Fast CPU ran the 6,300 frames checked; the attract demos play differently (the game's timing changes from frame 10).

verified.how: Workshop --wms-test (E6), 6,300 frames of the attract demos in lockstep with the SNES console: widescreen's centre 256 columns identical to the SNES picture every frame, STAT77 and the sound identical, switched off frame-identical; no flicker changes only lines over the SNES's limits; better sound changes only the sound.
